name: 210HL
typical_use: The 210HL from Cossor was listed in their 1935-6 manual and we have an advert for it from 1931. Cossor say of the 210HL that it probably the most popular valve in their battery series for use as a detector. Its characteristics are such as to suit it for use as a leaky grid detector in combination with small LF transformers. Under these conditions sufficient output is obtained to load a small output pentode or triode before overload occurs. In addition, the anode consumption is small, a consideration in receivers using HT batteries. The valve, in common with most other Cossor battery valves for use as HF or IF amplifiers, or as detectors, is fitted with seven point filament suspension. No microphony need therefore be feared as filament vibration is completely damped.

name: GU35
typical_use: Power Tetrode 3.5KW out, Heater 6.3V at 38 Amps.  5KV Anode Max

name: GZ34
typical_use: he GZ34 is an example of a typical high current rectifier for small equipment use.

name: KT61
typical_use: Beam Tetrode: The KT61 audio output valve, part of a series of very successful valves from M-OV, features the standard 6.3 Volt heater that was introduced from America in the mid 1930's.

name: L77/6C4
typical_use: The 6C4 triode valve was specified as both an amplifier and an RF power valve. In the latter role it would deliver 5.5 Watts in class C operation. With a very small envelope volume, this would make it ideal for hand portable equipment. In larger apparatus it could deliver enough drive power for much larger PA's.

name: N37
typical_use: The N37 is a television type audio output pentode. The load impedance is 6000 Ohms and the cathode resistor is 330 Ohms. At 10% total harmonic distortion the valve can produce 2.3 watts of audio.

name: OA2
typical_use: he 0A2 or OA2 is a cold cathode voltage stabiliser. The mean voltage stabilised is 150 Volts.

name: OB2
typical_use: The regulation of this tube was 3.5 Volts for currents of between 5 and 30 mA. So the voltage across this tube in service would have been held at between 106 and 110 Volts. The striking voltage was 133 Volts.

name: OV65
typical_use: The 1938 Pen25 battery output pentode from Mazda was designed for domestic broadcast receivers. The filament was to be run from accumulators and the 0.15 Amp filament current would have assisted in prolonging the accumulator life.

name: P646
typical_use: The EY87 is an EHT rectifier designed for EHT derived from the line timebase flyback. The DY87 has the same high voltage rating but has a 1.4 Volt 0.55 Amp heater. It is also for use in flyback generated EHT.

name: PC86
typical_use: The PC86 is a purpose designed UHF oscillator triode for television reception

name: PC88
typical_use: The PC88 is a UHF triode designed for grounded grid operation in the front end RF amplifier in Band IV and Band V television tuners

name: PC900
typical_use: The PC900 is a miniature VHF amplifier triode for use as an RF amplifier in television receivers. It is low impedance and has a high mutual conductance.

name: PC97
typical_use: The PC97 is a VHF triode. It has a high mutual conductance and could be used as a signal pre-amplifier.

name: PCC189
typical_use: The PCC189 is a low impedance high gain double triode for use as a cascode amplifier in television front-ends. It specifically states that it is built with frame grids. The valves are variable μ types for use at RF as AGC controlled devices.

name: PCC84
typical_use: The PCC84 double triode shows how valves developed to meet the needs of VHF television transmission. The PCC84 and PCF80 both featured in set-top converters for the new ITV television Band III channels that commenced broadcasting in 1955. The transmissions were on around 170 MHz and much higher in frequency than the BBC Band I signals at around 50 MHz.

name: PCF80
typical_use: The valve is a triode pentode, with separate cathodes, designed to function as a mixer and oscillator in the tuner.

name: PCF801
typical_use: The PCF801 is a television mixer oscillator. Triode pentode combinations worked better at high frequencies than hexode mixers.

name: PCF802
typical_use: The PCF802 was designed as the first stages in television line frequency generation prior to the line output stage. The pentode is described by Mullard as the oscillator while the triode is for service as a reactance valve. This suggests the triode acting as a frequency controlling stage.

name: PCF805
typical_use: purpose designed oscillator and mixer for frequency changer use in VHF television receivers.

name: PCF806
typical_use: triode and frame-grid pentode frequency changer for VHF television receivers up to 220 MHz.

name: PCF905
typical_use: No information, maybe PCF805 t is a purpose designed oscillator and mixer for frequency changer use in VHF television receivers.

name: PCH200
typical_use: triode heptode. The triode was designed as a pulse amplifier and the heptode section was designed for service as a noise gated sync. separator in colour television receivers.

name: PCH84
typical_use: The PCF84 is triode pentode oscillator and mixer for the front ends of VHF television sets.

name: PCL800
typical_use: Triode output pentode designed for field timebase or audio service. The PCL800 is a television receiver valve with a 300 mA heater for use with series heater chains. Domestic televisions worked at mains voltage and did not have a mains transformer.

name: PCL805
typical_use: triode pentode was purpose designed as a domestic television receiver frame output stage.

name: PCL805/85
typical_use: The PCL85 is a triode and output pentode combined.

name: PCL82
typical_use: The PCL82 triode pentode is typical of valve television receivers audio output stages

name: PCL83
typical_use: The PCL83 is a television triode output pentode. It is used as a frame timebase and frame output stage or audio output stage if required. It produces enough audio output power for an average domestic environment and was made from the early 1950s.

name: PCL84
typical_use: The PCL84 is a television triode and output pentode mainly for use as a video output stage.

name: PCL85
typical_use: The PCL85 is a triode and output pentode combined.

name: PCL86
typical_use: This PCL86 was made in the UK by Mullard and was designed for the audio stage of a television receiver and offered a quality output at about 4W. Pentode, Triode.

name: PF200
typical_use: The PFL200 combines a screened amplifier pentode and an output pentode in the one envelope. It was designed for television use, but probably not for audio output as the operating conditions do not give an output power. The mutual conductance of the output pentode at 21 is very high, pointing to a very small space between cathode and control grid.

name: PFL200
typical_use: two separate pentode valves in one package. For consumer electronics products cost reduction was vital, and the more functionality within each envelope the bette

name: PL504
typical_use: Pentode output valve -found their way into amateur radio transmitters for service at HF (up to 30 MHz) because of their peak voltage characteristics and relatively high current capability.

name: PL509
typical_use: The PL509 was one of the last TV line timebase output pentode valves to be designed. The PL519 replaced the PL509 and was pin compatible. These valves were designed for service in colour television receivers employing shadow mask tubes. The EL509 differs only in heater requirements. The normal anode voltage of 160 Volts is designed to be exceeded by pulses of up to 8,000 Volts and 1.4 Amps.

name: PL802
typical_use: purpose designed video output pentode for driving a cathode ray tube with the wide bandwidth signal needed for colour TV picture information. 300V at 6 watts

name: PL81
typical_use: The PL81 Line Ouput, 6KV was designed for universal mains sets without a mains transformer and with the heaters on a series chain. The parameters given are for a pair in push pull audio service.

name: PL82
typical_use: normally be found in audio stages of television receivers. A pair used in push pull class AB1 would deliver 9 Watts at 4 % distortion

name: PL83
typical_use: This is a true pentode with three wire grids. Used for video amplifier

name: PL84
typical_use: audio output pentode was designed for use in television receivers. Like the UL84 with a 100mA heater it is a low voltage high current version of the EL84, itself a standard in design.

name: PM1LF
typical_use: Type PM1LF was first introduced in 1926

name: PY33
typical_use: The PY33 is an HT rectifier for television receivers. It operates directly from the mains input and with a series resistance of 25 Ohms it will feed a reservoir capacitor of 200 µF.

name: PY80
typical_use: The PY80 is an early efficiency diode for television line scan systems and was part of the world series valves introduced by Mullard in 1950. The maximum peak inverse voltage on the anode has to be under 4 kV. The peak heater to cathode voltage has to be under 650 Volts.

name: PY800
typical_use: The PY800 was one of the last rectifiers of its type to be developed and is based on the PY81 from 1952. It was specifically built as an efficiency diode for television line scan in sets using 110° deflection angle tubes.

name: PY801
typical_use: The PY801 is a television efficiency diode for use in line timebase output circuits. Typically it will have a heater cathode insulation that is good to 6 kV and a peak current capability of 500 mA.

name: PY81
typical_use: The PY81 was specifically built as an efficiency diode for television line scan. The rectifier is specified as having a peak inverse voltage rating of 4,500 Volts, and a peak current rating of 450 mA.

name: PY81/800
typical_use: The PY80 is an early efficiency diode for television line scan systems and was part of the world series valves introduced by Mullard in 1950. Peak inverse voltage must be below 4KV

name: PY82
typical_use: The PY82 is an efficiency diode for use in domestic television receivers.

name: PY83
typical_use: The PY83 is an efficiency diode for use in television line scan circuits. The peak inverse anode voltage is 5,600 Volts and peak current is 500 mA.

name: PY88
typical_use: he PY88 is an efficiency diode for use in television line scan systems, where stored energy in the inductances is returned to the HT rail capacitors. The maximum peak inverse voltage (PIV) rating is 6,600 Volts. The peak anode current is 550 mA. These diodes require a very good heater cathode insulation and the PY88 is rated at 6,600 Volts.

name: QP22B
typical_use: The QP22B is a battery double pentode, designed for quiescent push pull class B audio amplification. Class B amplification produces considerable distortion at the points in the cycle where the valves move from cut-off to conduction. The advantage is that when not driven by a signal the power consumption from the HT battery is low. The total power output is 1 Watt and was aimed at driving a loudspeaker, quite a luxury when battery powered.

name: QQV02-6
typical_use: ouble beam tetrodes in this 1950s series from Mullard. It was introduced for 470 MHz (UHF) mobile transmitters.

name: QQV06-40
typical_use: ithin the envelope are two beam tetrodes with a maximum anode dissipation of 40 W.

name: QQV3-10
typical_use: double beam tetrode used in VHF transmitters

name: QS 150/15
typical_use: miniature voltage stabiliser. The striking voltage is 170 and for burning currents of 2 - 10 mA the regulation is 5 Volts.

name: TD22A
typical_use: 1934, The TDD2A is a double diode triode for battery receivers. The function was as detector, AGC rectifier and first audio voltage amplifier in a superhet broadcast receiver.

name: U191
typical_use: The U191 is a television efficiency diode. The function of the device is to enable the stored energy of the line scan coils to be returned to the supply rail during flyback.

name: U25
typical_use: The U25 is a dedicated television EHT rectifier for picture tube supplies. The Mullard code for this valve would be KY50 but U25 was the standard name. The valve is rated at 19 kV peak inverse volts

name: U26
typical_use: purpose designed EHT rectifier for monochrome television picture tube supplies. The U26

name: U282
typical_use: The U282 is a television efficiency diode, used to return energy from the collapsing field in the line coils to the HT rail. The peak current is given as 600 mA

name: U319
typical_use: U319 is a half wave rectifier designed for 300 mA heater chain equipment.

name: UABC80
typical_use: The UABC80 is a triple diode triode

name: UAF42
typical_use: The UAF42 is an early all glass valve introduced in 1948 together with the EAF42 and consists of a single diode and a variable μ RF amplifier pentode in a single envelope.

name: UBC41
typical_use: The UBC41 is an early all glass valve and less clear or free from imperfections than later valves. This is a double diode triode valve on a B8B base. Mullard describe the UBC41 as a high gain triode for use as an AF voltage amplifier, combined with twin diodes, for DC/AC mains operation.

name: UBC81
typical_use: small double diode triode was designed for signal demodulation and AGC detection in universal mains domestic equipment. The triode section could be used for a first stage of amplification after the detection process.

name: UCC85
typical_use: The UCC85 is the universal supply version of the ECC85 VHF double triode, designed for RF amplifier and local oscillator use in FM radio receivers.

name: UCH42
typical_use: The UCH42 is an early all glass triode hexode from 1948 and was designed as oscillator and mixer for superhet receivers, and the hexode section was designed to operate with an AGC control voltage.

name: UCL83
equivalents: The UCL83 is an AF amplifier triode and an output pentode combined in a single envelope. The use would have been for post detector amplification and loudspeaker driving in broadcast receivers and small VHF televisions sets. The 100 mA heater is for use on heater chains in universal AC or DC mains equipment

name: UF41
typical_use: he UF41 from Mullard is a vari-mu amplifier pentode. Use was for AGC controlled RF and IF amplification in superhet receivers

name: UL41
typical_use: The UL41 is an audio output pentode from 1953. The U series were designed to operate with a heater chain across the mains in the days when AC mains had not reached all parts of the country. These universal sets contained no mains transformers and the valves were designed for low anode voltage and higher anode current to provide adequate output. The UL41 could produce 4.2 Watts at 10% distortion.

name: UL84
typical_use: The Mullard EL84 is a classic audio pentode valve, immortalised in the 1950s 5-10 design for an audio amplifier. The UL84 was designed with a 100 mA heater, for use in universal voltage environments and thus with limited HT available. Our exhibit carries the Mullard logo but was not of UK manufacture.On a DC mains supply no transformer to increase the HT voltage is possible so the UL84 is designed to operate at lower anode voltages and increased anode current.

name: UY41
typical_use: The UY41 is a half wave rectifier designed for universal domestic equipment and replaced the UY21. By universal we mean AC or DC mains input and therefore no mains transformer.

name: UY85
typical_use: The UY85 is a half wave rectifier and would be used on small universal (AC/DC) mains appliances. The heater chain would draw 100 mA and this was to enable the small number of valves used in a broadcast radio receiver to be run without a large dropper (ballast) resister.

name: VR 105/30
typical_use: old cathode voltage stabiliser. The details of its operation are given in the type designation. This tube will stabilise the voltage across it to 105 Volts for output currents between 5 mA and 30 mA. To strike the tube the voltage must exceed 135 V.

name: VR-150
typical_use: The VR150 is a gas filled discharge tube that exhibits a near constant voltage across the valve for currents within the range 5mA to 40mA. In fact the regulation is 150 plus or minus 5.5 Volts.

name: Z329
typical_use: The Z329 is a miniature screened pentode that was designed to operate at the standard TV intermediate frequency of 33 MHz. The IF stages in any superhet receiver are where the main signal voltage amplification takes place.

name: Z749
typical_use: The Z749 is a screened amplifier pentode, the GEC name was used as the professional brand of M-OV. The Z749 is directly equivalent to the EF812 and closely related to the EF80. TV and radar receivers would require wide bandwidth RF amplification.

name: Z759
typical_use: The Z759 is an RF pentode with a high mutual conductance designed for video or other wideband RF amplification.
